findings.impact: The most common regenerate case, a file with both a short and a detailed summary, could regress unnoticed: 'Create again' returns 200, the worker's _has_summary sees the old text and skips, and the user silently keeps the old summary with no error.

findings.claim: Batch classification now counts a file with only a vision placeholder row as missing a summary, so an image previously reported as skipped is reported as queued although the worker never generates anything for it.
findings.impact: Running 'Create AI summaries' on a folder containing described images can report 'Added N summaries to the queue' on every run instead of 'All files already have summaries', and nothing appears for those files.

specification_compliance: No invariants file, and therefore no touch-point list, exists for this change, and no spec under docs/ mentions the detailed-only fix, so the question 'which places does the diff reach outside the touch-point list' has no list to compare against.

Taking the removed known-issues entry as the only statement of intent, it names GET /summary and the batch run. The diff also changes POST /summary/regenerate (summaries.py:290-311), which that entry does not name. This is the one place reached beyond it. The change looks deliberate: it has a comment and a test, and the old unconditional DELETE dropped detailed_status, which makes enqueue_unprocessed's detailed gap (workers/summaries.py:1316-1319) and _has_detailed_summary treat the file as having no detailed summary.

The known-issues removal matches the code: GET (summaries.py:226-227) and batch (summaries.py:539-540) now read the short text through _HAS_SHORT_SUMMARY, the same predicate as _has_summary and enqueue_unprocessed.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Regenerate on a row with detailed_status set now keeps the row and clears the short/long columns in place, rather than deleting it. Visual-description columns on such a row also survive, while a row with detailed_status NULL is still deleted along with any visual-description columns.

POST /summary/edit and /summary/revert on a row cleared by regenerate find the row, whereas after the old DELETE edit returned 404 'No summary to edit'. An edit there succeeds while status stays 'hidden' and writes short_original='' as the snapshot.
regression_risks: A stale panel can reach edit on a cleared row: SummarySection.handleRegenerate (frontend/SummarySection.tsx:96-119) only updates data when polling succeeds, so if regeneration fails, old data may remain client-side. An edit would then succeed on a status='hidden' row, and metadata.py:245 omits long_summary from the embedding for hidden rows. decisions.md reports the panel section disappearing in the failure case, so this path may not be reachable through the UI.

The predicate is duplicated: indexer.py:1044 still spells out COALESCE(short_summary, '') != '' instead of using _HAS_SHORT_SUMMARY, so a later change to one would diverge from the other. This is pre-existing and not touched by the diff.
GET /summary filters with the unqualified short_summary in a join with indexed_files, which would become ambiguous if indexed_files ever gained a column of that name.
test_coverage: GET by short text (empty and non-empty) and batch queue/skip by short text are covered with a real SQLite DB in TestRowWithoutShortSummary; removing _HAS_SHORT_SUMMARY from either query should fail those tests.

Regenerate on a detailed-only row is covered for keeping detailed_status and clearing edited_at and short_original. Clearing of short_summary, long_summary, status and long_original is not effectively asserted (F1).
The DELETE branch's predicate has no real-DB coverage (F2).

The chosen-profile regenerate path shares _delete and is covered only by the recording fake. No test covers a row with detailed_status='generating' or 'failed' in regenerate, although the predicate treats them the same as 'generated'.
